speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I can see you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance. To help me understand your condition better, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually, and have you noticed any hearing loss or ringing in your ears?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see that diphenhydramine helped slightly; have you noticed any nystagmus (involuntary eye movements), facial weakness, or difficulty speaking along with your dizziness? REQUEST TEST: Audiometry

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Basic Audiometry: Bilateral decreased hearing sensitivity, details not specified.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sustained sensation of the room spinning. I also have Occasional nausea, Use of diphenhydramine for symptoms and to aid sleep, Recent cold. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vestibular Neuritis (with likely prior viral labyrinthitis given the "recent cold" and lack of hearing loss, ruling out MS which typically presents with other neurological deficits and does not resolve so quickly). The patient's history of a recent cold, unilateral constant vertigo without hearing loss or central neurological signs (nystagmus, facial weakness) strongly points to an inner ear inflammation rather than Multiple Sclerosis. I will confirm the diagnosis with a vestibular function test and request images to rule out posterior fossa pathology despite the low probability. REQUEST TEST: Video Head Impulse Test (vHIT). REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with focus on Internal Auditory Canals and Posterior Fossa.
